title: The effects of over-reliance on AI dialogue systems on students’ cognitive abilities: a systematic review
extended_summary:
This paper examines the growing concern that students may over-rely on AI dialogue systems, especially generative tools used in academic research and writing, and that such dependence may weaken key cognitive abilities. The review focuses on three cognitive domains: decision-making, critical thinking, and analytical thinking. It also identifies the ethical issues that the authors argue contribute to over-reliance, including hallucination, algorithmic bias, plagiarism, privacy concerns, and lack of transparency.

The study is a systematic review following PRISMA procedures. The authors searched four databases (ProQuest, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science) for English-language journal articles and conference proceedings published from 2017 to 2023. After screening, 14 studies were included in the synthesis. The included evidence largely concerns higher education contexts, with student users and some educator/faculty perspectives, especially around academic writing, paraphrasing, and research assistance.

Across the reviewed studies, AI dialogue systems were found to offer practical benefits such as faster research, writing support, immediate feedback, and personalized assistance. However, the paper concludes that these benefits come with important risks: users may become overly dependent on AI-generated outputs, which can reduce independent judgment, creativity, and critical/analytical reasoning. The review argues that ethical weaknesses in AI systems, rather than the tools alone, are central drivers of over-reliance and that more responsible use is needed to protect cognitive development and academic integrity.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI/chatbot system used for generating and interacting with natural-language outputs.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper reviewed studies that used ChatGPT/GPT-4 and related GPT-based dialogue systems in research and education, especially for academic writing, paraphrasing, scientific questions, and feedback support.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT was reported to improve efficiency in academic writing and research tasks, streamline workflows, and provide immediate feedback or 24/7 availability. However, the review also synthesized concerns that over-reliance on ChatGPT may reduce critical thinking, analytical thinking, creativity, and decision-making, and may increase plagiarism, hallucination, bias, and transparency problems.
findings.measure: Synthesized outcomes from included studies on writing efficiency, feedback, and cognitive/ethical risks
findings.sample_size: 14 studies reviewed; tool-specific sample sizes varied and were not pooled

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that ChatGPT can support academic writing, help overcome language barriers, and improve writing productivity. At the same time, it may contribute to reduced originality and writing dependence, with some included studies warning about academic dishonesty and plagiarism risks.
findings.measure: Synthesized outcomes on academic writing support and writing quality
findings.sample_size: 14 studies reviewed; tool-specific sample sizes varied and were not pooled

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review synthesizing 14 articles, but it does not provide pooled effect sizes or a single controlled evaluation of ChatGPT. The evidence is mainly descriptive and mixed-method in nature, so it does not meet blue/green experimental standards.
impact_tier_rationale: The review suggests meaningful potential benefits for writing efficiency and feedback, but also substantial risks to critical thinking and academic integrity. Because no quantified effect size is reported, impact is best characterized as promising but unclear.
